ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حم (١) تَنْزِيلٌ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ (٢) كِتَابٌ فُصِّلَتْ آيَاتُهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ (٣)).
His saying (تَنْزِيلٌ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ): it is like the beginning of al-Sajda. كِتَابٌ: i.e. "it is a Book". It may also be nominative by تَنْزِيلٌ, i.e. "a Book has been sent down"; or a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, or a badal (substitute). And (قُرْآنًا) is a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa, circumstantial) of «آيَاتُهُ». It may also be a ḥāl of «كِتَابٌ», because it has been qualified [by an adjective].

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ مِنْ فَوْقِهَا وَبَارَكَ فِيهَا وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَا أَقْوَاتَهَا فِي أَرْبَعَةِ أَيَّامٍ سَوَاءً لِلسَّائِلِينَ (١٠)).
His saying (وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا): it is resumptive, not conjoined to «خَلَقَ», because if it were conjoined to it, it would fall within the ṣila (relative clause); and that is not permissible, because the two have been separated by His saying (وَتَجْعَلُونَ...) to the end of the verse, which is in no way part of the ṣila.
His saying (فِي أَرْبَعَةِ أَيَّامٍ): i.e. "in the completion of four days". Were it not for this implied wording, the days would be eight: two days in the first, which is His saying (خَلَقَ الْأَرْضَ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ), and two days in the last, which is His saying (فَقَضَاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ).
(سَوَاءً), in the accusative: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they became equal, an equalling"; and it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «أَقْوَاتَهَا», or of that in فِيهَا, or of الْأَرْضَ. It is also read in the genitive (سَوَاءٍ) as a naʿt (adjective) of الْأَيَّامِ, and in the nominative (سَوَاءٌ) on the implied wording "they are equal".

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلْأَرْضِ اِئْتِيَا طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًا قَالَتَا أَتَيْنَا طَائِعِينَ (١١)).
His saying (اِئْتِيَا): i.e. "come, both of you". And (طَوْعًا) and (كَرْهًا) are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).
And (أَتَيْنَا) with the short vowel, i.e. "we have come"; and with the long vowel (آتَيْنَا), i.e. "we have given obedience from ourselves".
And (طَائِعِينَ) is a ḥāl; it is plural [in the masculine form of rational beings] because He described them with the attributes of those who have reason; or the implied wording is "we have come with whoever is in us", and for that reason it is plural.
It is also said: it is plural according to the multiplicity of the heavens and the earth.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t: Allah the Exalted said: (فَقَضَاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ فِي يَوْمَيْنِ وَأَوْحَى فِي كُلِّ سَمَاءٍ أَمْرَهَا وَزَيَّنَّا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا بِمَصَابِيحَ وَحِفْظًا ذَلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ (١٢)) (وَحِفْظًا): i.e. "and We guarded it with a guarding" (mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object), or "for guarding".

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ جَاءَتْهُمُ الرُّسُلُ مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ قَالُوا لَوْ شَاءَ رَبُّنَا لَأَنْزَلَ مَلَائِكَةً فَإِنَّا بِمَا أُرْسِلْتُمْ بِهِ كَافِرُونَ (١٤)).
(إِذْ جَاءَتْهُمُ): it may be an adverb of time for أَنْذَرْتُكُمْ, as you say "I met you when such-and-such was the case"; or it may be a naʿt (adjective) of صَاعِقَةً, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the second «صَاعِقَةِ».

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا فِي أَيَّامٍ نَحِسَاتٍ لِنُذِيقَهُمْ عَذَابَ الْخِزْيِ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَلَعَذَابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَخْزَى وَهُمْ لَا يُنْصَرُونَ (١٦)).
His saying (نَحِسَاتٍ): it is read with kasra on the ḥāʾ, and there are two views on it:
The first: it is an active participle, like نَصِبٌ and نَصِبَاتٌ. The second: that it was originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الْكَلِمَةُ. It is also read with sukūn (نَحْسَاتٍ), and there are two views on it:
The first: it has the meaning of the form with kasra, and was made quiescent only for an incidental reason.
The second: that it was originally an active participle, made quiescent for lightness.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ فَاسْتَحَبُّوا الْعَمَى عَلَى الْهُدَى فَأَخَذَتْهُمْ صَاعِقَةُ الْعَذَابِ الْهُونِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ (١٧))
His saying (وَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ): it is in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ» is the khabar (predicate). And in the accusative (ثَمُودَ) by an omitted verb, its implied form being "as for Thamūd, We guided [them]", explained by His saying «فَهَدَيْنَاهُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَوْمَ يُحْشَرُ أَعْدَاءُ اللَّهِ إِلَى النَّارِ فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ (١٩))
His saying (وَيَوْمَ يُحْشَرُ): it is an adverb of time for what is indicated by what comes after it, which is
His saying «فَهُمْ يُوزَعُونَ»; as though He said: "they will be held back on the day We gather".

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَتِرُونَ أَنْ يَشْهَدَ عَلَيْكُمْ سَمْعُكُمْ وَلَا أَبْصَارُكُمْ وَلَا جُلُودُكُمْ وَلَكِنْ ظَنَنْتُمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَعْلَمُ كَثِيرًا مِمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ (٢٢)).
His saying (أَنْ يَشْهَدَ): i.e. "from [the possibility] that it would testify" (مِنْ أَنْ يَشْهَدَ), because تَسْتَتِرُ is not transitive by itself.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَذَلِكُمْ ظَنُّكُمُ الَّذِي ظَنَنْتُمْ بِرَبِّكُمْ أَرْدَاكُمْ فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ (٢٣)).
His saying (وَذَلِكُمْ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «ظَنُّكُمْ» is its khabar (predicate); «الَّذِي» is a naʿt (adjective) of the khabar, or a khabar after a khabar; and «أَرْدَاكُمْ» is a further khabar.
It may also be that all of them are naʿt or badal (substitute), and «أَرْدَاكُمْ» is the khabar.
It may also be that «أَرْدَاكُمْ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «قَدْ» intended along with it.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنْ يَصْبِرُوا فَالنَّارُ مَثْوًى لَهُمْ وَإِنْ يَسْتَعْتِبُوا فَمَا هُمْ مِنَ الْمُعْتَبِينَ (٢٤)).
His saying (يَسْتَعْتِبُوا): it is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the second tāʾ, i.e. "that they ask for the removal of what they are reproached for". (فَمَا هُمْ مِنَ الْمُعْتَبِينَ): with fatḥa on the tāʾ, i.e. "among those whose request for the removal of reproach is granted".
It is also read «يُسْتَعْتَبُوا», with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the tāʾ, i.e. "what they are not reproached for is asked of them"; and then فَمَا هُمْ مِنَ الْمُعْتِبِينَ with kasra on the tāʾ, i.e. "among those who remove reproach".

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَذَا الْقُرْآنِ وَالْغَوْا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ (٢٦)).
His saying (وَالْغَوْا فِيهِ): it is read with fatḥa on the ghayn, from لَغَا يَلْغَى, and with ḍamma on it (وَالْغُوا), from لَغَا يَلْغُو; the meaning is the same.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ أَعْدَاءِ اللَّهِ النَّارُ لَهُمْ فِيهَا دَارُ الْخُلْدِ جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا يَجْحَدُونَ (٢٨)).
His saying (النَّارُ): it is a badal (substitute) of جَزَاءُ, or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or a mubtadaʾ with what follows it as the khabar. And (جَزَاءً) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they were requited with that, a requital".
It may also be accusative by جَزَاءُ أَعْدَاءِ اللَّهِ, or a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقَامُوا تَتَنَزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ أَلَّا تَخَافُوا وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا وَأَبْشِرُوا بِالْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ (٣٠)).
His saying (أَلَّا تَخَافُوا): the implied wording may be "with [the message] that you should not fear" (بِأَنْ لَا تَخَافُوا), or "saying: do not fear". [On the first, it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they descend with their saying "do not fear"; on the second, the ḥāl is omitted.]

ukberi-tibyan:31-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (نَحْنُ أَوْلِيَاؤُكُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَا تَشْتَهِي أَنْفُسُكُمْ وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَا تَدَّعُونَ (٣١) نُزُلًا مِنْ غَفُورٍ رَحِيمٍ (٣٢))
His saying (نُزُلًا): there are two views on it. The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted hāʾ [i.e. the object pronoun of تَدَّعُونَ], or of مَا; i.e. "yours is what you call for, prepared", and the like; and «مِنْ» is a naʿt (adjective) of it. The second: it is the plural of نَازِلٌ, like صَابِرٌ and صُبُرٌ; so it is a ḥāl of the wāw in «تَدَّعُونَ», or of the kāf and mīm in «لَكُمْ». On this view مِنْ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to تَدَّعُونَ, i.e. "they ask for it from One Forgiving"; or to the adverbial phrase, i.e. "that is settled from One Forgiving", so that it is a ḥāl of «مَا».

ukberi-tibyan:34-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَسْتَوِي الْحَسَنَةُ وَلَا السَّيِّئَةُ ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ فَإِذَا الَّذِي بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُ عَدَاوَةٌ كَأَنَّهُ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمٌ (٣٤) وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَمَا يُلَقَّاهَا إِلَّا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ (٣٥)).
His saying (كَأَنَّهُ وَلِيٌّ): there are two views on it:
The first: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الَّذِي» together with its ṣila (relative clause), and «الَّذِي» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); إِذَا is [the إِذَا] of surprise, and «هِيَ» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: so in the text («هِيَ», "it"); evidently «إِذَا» is meant, i.e. إِذَا of surprise is the khabar]; i.e. "and there, present, is the enemy, resembling a friend"; and the benefit [of the statement] is obtained from the ḥāl.
The second: that it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and «إِذَا» is an adverb of time for the meaning of likening; an adverb may precede an abstract governor (ʿāmil maʿnawī).
The pronoun in «يُلَقَّاهَا» refers to the trait or to the word.

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ اللَّيْلُ وَالنَّهَارُ وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ لَا تَسْجُدُوا لِلشَّمْسِ وَلَا لِلْقَمَرِ وَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ (٣٧)).
His saying (خَلَقَهُنَّ): the pronoun refers to the signs, which are the night, the day, the sun and the moon.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِالذِّكْرِ لَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ وَإِنَّهُ لَكِتَابٌ عَزِيزٌ (٤١)).
His saying (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ» is omitted, i.e. "are obstinate" or "are perishing". It is also said: it is (أُولَئِكَ يُنَادَوْنَ).

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ قُرْآنًا أَعْجَمِيًّا لَقَالُوا لَوْلَا فُصِّلَتْ آيَاتُهُ أَأَعْجَمِيٌّ وَعَرَبِيٌّ قُلْ هُوَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هُدًى وَشِفَاءٌ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ فِي آذَانِهِمْ وَقْرٌ وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى أُولَئِكَ يُنَادَوْنَ مِنْ مَكَانٍ بَعِيدٍ (٤٤)).
His saying (أَأَعْجَمِيٌّ): it is a question.
It is also read with a single hamza and fatḥa on the ʿayn (أَعَجَمِيٌّ), as a relative adjective (nisba) to عَجَمٌ.
And (عَمًى) is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of عَمِيَ, like صَدِيَ صَدًى. It is also read with kasra on the mīm (عَمٍ), i.e. "obscure", so it is an active participle. It is also read عَمِيَ, as a past verb. So عَلَى is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the active participle or to the verb.
As for the maṣdar, it cannot be attached to it because it precedes it; but it may be by way of clarification (tabyīn), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَنْ عَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ أَسَاءَ فَعَلَيْهَا وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ (٤٦)).
His saying (فَلِنَفْسِهِ): it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then it is for his own self".

ukberi-tibyan:47-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَيْهِ يُرَدُّ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ وَمَا تَخْرُجُ مِنْ ثَمَرَاتٍ مِنْ أَكْمَامِهَا وَمَا تَحْمِلُ مِنْ أُنْثَى وَلَا تَضَعُ إِلَّا بِعِلْمِهِ وَيَوْمَ يُنَادِيهِمْ أَيْنَ شُرَكَائِي قَالُوا آذَنَّاكَ مَا مِنَّا مِنْ شَهِيدٍ (٤٧) وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يَدْعُونَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَظَنُّوا مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ (٤٨))
His saying (وَمَا تَحْمِلُ): «مَا» is negating, because «وَلَا تَضَعُ» is conjoined to it and then the negation is broken by إِلَّا; if it had the sense of الَّذِي (that which), conjoined to السَّاعَةِ, that would not be sound. As for
His saying (وَمَا تَخْرُجُ مِنْ ثَمَرَاتٍ), it may have the sense of الَّذِي, but the stronger view is that it is negating.
His saying (آذَنَّاكَ): this verb is transitive to one object by itself and to another by a preposition; here the negation and what falls in its domain occupy the place of the preposition and its genitive noun. Abū Ḥātim said: one pauses at آذَنَّاكَ and then begins anew; so the negation has no grammatical position.
As for His saying (وَظَنُّوا): its two objects are dispensed with by (مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ). Abū Ḥātim said: one pauses at «ظَنُّوا», and then a statement is made about them with the negation.

ukberi-tibyan:49-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا يَسْأَمُ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ دُعَاءِ الْخَيْرِ وَإِنْ مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ فَيَئُوسٌ قَنُوطٌ (٤٩) وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْنَاهُ رَحْمَةً مِنَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ ضَرَّاءَ مَسَّتْهُ لَيَقُولَنَّ هَذَا لِي وَمَا أَظُنُّ السَّاعَةَ قَائِمَةً وَلَئِنْ رُجِعْتُ إِلَى رَبِّي إِنَّ لِي عِنْدَهُ لَلْحُسْنَى فَلَنُنَبِّئَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِمَا عَمِلُوا وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ مِنْ عَذَابٍ غَلِيظٍ (٥٠)).
And (دُعَاءِ الْخَيْرِ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in construct with its object, the agent being omitted. And (لَيَقُولَنَّ هَذَا لِي) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with the fāʾ omitted.
It is also said: it is the answer to an omitted oath.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالُوا قُلُوبُنَا فِي أَكِنَّةٍ مِمَّا تَدْعُونَا إِلَيْهِ وَفِي آذَانِنَا وَقْرٌ وَمِنْ بَيْنِنَا وَبَيْنِكَ حِجَابٌ فَاعْمَلْ إِنَّنَا عَامِلُونَ (٥)).
His saying (مِمَّا تَدْعُونَا): it is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning of «فِي أَكِنَّةٍ» is "veiled from hearing what you call us to". It cannot be a naʿt (adjective) of أَكِنَّةٍ, because الْأَكِنَّةُ are the coverings, and the coverings are not part of what you call us to.

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَاتِنَا فِي الْآفَاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ (٥٣)).
His saying (بِرَبِّكَ): the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and it is the fāʿil (agent) of يَكْفِي, with the object omitted, i.e. "does your Lord not suffice you?". On this view «أَنَّهُ» is in the position of a badal (substitute) of the agent, either according to the wording or according to the position; i.e. "does your Lord — His witnessing — not suffice you?".
It is also said: it is in the position of the accusative [or the genitive, on the implied wording بِأَنَّهُ ("in that He…"). It is also said: «بِرَبِّكَ» is in the accusative position], as the object of يَكْفِي; i.e. "does His witnessing not suffice your Lord?".

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ (٨)).
And (مَمْنُونٍ) is a passive participle, from مَنَنْتُ الْحَبْلَ, i.e. "I cut the rope".
